To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a deep neural network trained on text and image features can achieve state-of-the-art performance in document classification, (ii) the proposed multimodal network can learn the most discriminative features by fusing text and image features, and (iii) the proposed network outperforms other state-of-the-art document classifiers.

(1) we introduce a new multimodal neural network, (2) we introduce a novel text dataset that we use to augment existing datasets, and (3) we show that this new approach outperforms the state of the art.

(a) we propose an approach to combine text and images to improve document classification; (b) we introduce a dataset of 3482 documents with 12 classes; and (c) we propose a multimodal neural architecture to combine text and image features.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) What is the best way to combine visual and textual information for document classification?
the following contributions: (1) we introduce a new OCR text dataset, QS OCR, which is a collection of scanned documents and their clean text versions.
the following questions: 1) How can we design deep neural networks that can effectively learn from both text and image information?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multimodal deep learning is the best approach for document classification.
the proposed approach is a good candidate to classify documents in a real-world setting.
our proposed method outperforms the current state of the art on Tobacco3482 by 3.5% and RVL CDip by 4.3% on the validation set and 2.5% on Tobacco3483.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our multimodal approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods for document image classification.

we show that a multimodal deep learning approach is able to achieve a better performance than the state-of-the-art in the field, and that it can be used in the real world setting, where text and visual information can be extracted with reasonable accuracy.
we have designed a new multimodal deep neural network that is capable of learning from the text content of the documents as well as from their visual appearance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
text and images are complementary and that the combination of both modalities is essential to obtain the best performance.
the combination of visual and textual information can boost the performance of document image classification, and can be achieved with simple neural network architectures.
the multimodal approach is a promising direction to achieve high accuracy in document classification.
